topology: PC1 and PC2 share a prepared VLAN1 access switch and R1 client LAN. R1 has separate SRV1 HTTP and SRV2 DNS/HTTP LANs. Manual dual-stack addressing, scoped IPv6 default gateways and services are prepared; R1 IPv6 forwarding initially starts disabled.
implemented: Fifth ENCOR Security lab and37 ENCOR entries. Existing CCNA ACL and AAA labs remain available; shared links retain the current domain, path and query.
Native IOS named IPv6 ACL trailing sequence syntax, no sequence editing, seven ordered EDGE-V6 entries, exclusive Gi0/0 inbound ipv6 traffic-filter and visible interface binding output.

IPv6 TCP destination80 host exception, UDP53 client-prefix permission, ICMPv6 echo permission, broader server deny and explicit terminal deny. Full HTTP200 responses, fresh receiver-confirmed AAAA answers and three correlated ACL-permitted echo replies prove the actual services and forwarding.

Incoming logical IPv6 Neighbor Solicitation/Advertisement now pass through the applied interface ACL before cache learning and DAD observation. Explicit nd-ns/nd-na permissions preserve resolution; a terminal deny overrides the classic IOS implicit ND exception. Unsolicited advertisements map to the all-nodes multicast destination.

The positive neighbor exercise requires a real PC1 gateway solicitation and a separately solicited advertisement, with actual received NDP frame IDs; background DAD and gratuitous announcements alone cannot earn it.

Cold gateway failure requires an actual denied solicitation for fe80::1, followed by a newly permitted solicitation and three fresh successfully filtered replies after restoring both ND entries. Warm cache success cannot substitute.

Explicit versus implicit deny, first-match shadowing, wrong HTTP source/destination ports, wrong DNS protocol/port, returning echo-reply egress filtering and temporarily unbound access are verified with actual packet evidence. Repair requires new traffic after the fault.
A fresh PC2 IPv4 HTTP success after the corresponding IPv6 denial proves address-family independence.

clear ipv6 access-list [name] clears IPv6 counters while retaining IPv4 counts. A bounded reset history records actual pre-clear counts. Lab credit requires the populated named list and fresh permitted/denied traffic after clearing; empty, unrelated and all-list clears cannot substitute.

Final live save checks exact restored IPv6 policy/binding, IPv4/IPv6 forwarding, startup equality, original addresses and both host gateway families, services/AAAA data, operational access VLAN1 paths and five healthy links without extra filters.

Practice begins0/20. Completed reference has four live tasks with empty serialized runtime; boot-time DAD/ND rebuilds naturally and cannot invent traffic, repair or reset achievements. All20 earned outcomes survive YAML export/import while runtime sessions and counters rebuild.
Bounded imported criteria reject unknown checks, foreign roots and missing required interfaces. Cached DNS, fabricated counters and advisory ACL queries alone do not create traffic evidence.
scope: Working IOS routed IPv6 interface ACLs and logical incoming NS/NA decisions. The seven-entry reference explicitly permits ND before its terminal deny so the exercise does not depend on platform-specific implicit ND defaults.
Binary ND wire encoding, outgoing locally generated NDP ACL filtering, fragmentation matching, ACL log aggregation, scheduled ACLs and stateful inspection are not configured or certified by this lab.
Primary Cisco documentation reviewed. No new live CML capture was performed. Existing IOS/NX-OS CML regression contracts pass within the full suite.
No UI layout/theme, terminal styling, artwork, dependency or server/backend changes.
